robot: Unitree H1-2 humanoid, 27 joints (legs 12, torso 1, arms 7 + 7), 1.78 m; Unitree's walking policy built in; fist pads on both wrists

frame.suite: heading only: the yaw of the pelvis IMU in the venue's world frame; the robot senses no position, so x and y stay 0
frame.base_text: the robot base frame: on the floor under the pelvis, +X the way the pelvis faces at the start of the call, +Y left, +Z up (only the heading is sensed, from the pelvis IMU)

torso.note: the torso (yaw), joint targets through the stand type

left.note: 7 joints: shoulder pitch, roll, yaw, elbow pitch, elbow roll, wrist pitch, wrist yaw; joint targets through the stand type

right.note: 7 joints: shoulder pitch, roll, yaw, elbow pitch, elbow roll, wrist pitch, wrist yaw; joint targets through the stand type

legs.note: 12 joints (left hip yaw, pitch, roll, knee, ankle pitch, roll; then the right leg's) through the joints type: the default gains, nothing balances the robot

locomotion.note: Unitree's H1-2 walking policy (`walk` rows at 50 Hz; the torso and arms keep their targets): at the largest forward command (0.8) it walks about 0.6 m/s and its heading drifts (check the heading in the state); at zero command it marks time on the spot; moving the arms disturbs it. Coming from another mode it first blends the legs to its stance (0.3 s) and holds still until steady (up to 2 s). Each call ends with 1 s of zero command. This robot has no running policy.

resets.note: Embodied Olympics allows 5 resets (describe_robot: resets): each starts a new attempt from the same start; only the last attempt is graded, and a success ends the run.

notes: Joint targets are absolute angles (rad); a target moves at most the joint's speed limit per 10 ms step. The arms (left, right) and the torso take joint targets through the `stand` action type: the platform holds the legs in the standing stance with stiff gains and gravity support but no balance feedback, so a fast or hard arm swing can tip the robot over; a move_robot call on these parts switches the legs back to `stand`. The legs part uses the `joints` type (every joint at the default gains; nothing balances the robot in that mode). Legs and arm goals use different action types: send them in separate move_robot calls, or send rows of any of the robot's action types with execute_trajectory space native (stand, walk, joints, lowcmd; layouts and bounds in describe_robot). move_robot and joint rows for the arms and the torso start from the last `stand` row sent through these tools (at the start of an attempt: the start command), grips included; locomote and the legs part start from the joint targets in force and keep a grip closed while that hand holds something (holding_* in proprio_now), open otherwise. On a fist pad a grip of 0.5 or more closes it (it holds a grippable object within 3.5 cm of the palm). Between calls the robot is frozen: time passes only inside calls. There is no end-effector pose command: describe_robot's spec_file (robot_facts) has each joint's range, speed and torque limits, default gains and the stance. The robot senses no position: the state shows its heading (the pelvis IMU's yaw) only, and locomote's displacement reports the turn (dyaw), while dx and dy stay 0: judge distances from the cameras. Once an attempt is over, results carry the referee's call (outcome, stages_reached of stages_total).
